scope: Schedule 1 H2 — Wastewater treatment systems and cesspools (conditional)
Schedule 1 H5 — Separate systems of drainage (conditional)

sourceSnapshots.title: Approved Document H — Drainage and waste disposal
sourceSnapshots.authorityNote: Compliance guidance, not the statutory requirement itself.

sourceSnapshots.title: Water Industry Act 1991 — section 106 right to communicate with public sewers
sourceSnapshots.authorityNote: Separate sewerage-law authority. DPL-09C does not treat this source as a Building Regulations requirement or as proof that a particular connection is technically available.

sourceSnapshots.title: General binding rules for small sewage discharges with effect from 2 October 2023
sourceSnapshots.authorityNote: Separate environmental-permitting regime relevant only if a non-mains small sewage discharge is proposed. It does not replace H1/H2.

methodClasses.claimBoundary: Determines only whether a conditional drainage obligation is triggered from admitted facts. Missing network/site facts remain unresolved.
Competent drainage/civil design and hydraulic evidence are required. Architectural topology or target routing does not establish adequacy.
Sewer maps, surveyed asset facts, undertaker determinations/consents and rights evidence remain external. A planning drawing or listing does not discharge this method.
Ground/permeability/groundwater/contamination evidence and competent infiltration design are required before infiltration can be treated as adequate or reasonably practicable.
Non-mains sewage/environmental discharge legality and permits/general-binding-rule compliance remain with the applicable environmental regime and evidence.

obligations.title: Adequate foul-water drainage and disposal route
requiredInputs: public/private sewer evidence and connection position where relevant
evidence supporting whether each higher-priority route is reasonably practicable
priorityOrder: private sewer communicating with a public sewer where public sewer is not reasonably practicable
septic tank with appropriate secondary treatment or other wastewater treatment system where sewer routes are not reasonably practicable
cesspool where preceding routes are not reasonably practicable
obligations.nonClaim: The priority order is statutory, but whether a particular route is reasonably practicable is not inferred from absence/presence of a map symbol or from architectural preference.

obligations.title: Wastewater treatment system / septic tank / cesspool adequacy
requiredInputs: environmental-permitting/general-binding-rule evidence where the system discharges to ground or surface water
obligations.nonClaim: H2 applicability does not authorise or environmentally permit a non-mains discharge.

obligations.title: Adequate provision to carry rainwater from the roof
requiredInputs: actual roof catchments and finished falls
design rainfall / selected lawful technical method
partialNativeEvidence: DRW-10C inspectable perimeter collection and outward-failure analytical evidence
obligations.nonClaim: Controlled roof-water topology does not establish H3 hydraulic adequacy.

obligations.title: Adequate drainage of applicable paved areas around the building
requiredInputs: whether the paved area falls within the H3(2) application conditions
obligations.nonClaim: The presence of a conceptual step-free approach does not by itself prove the final H3(2) paved-area design.

obligations.title: Rainwater discharge route priority
requiredInputs: whether rainwater is gathered for reuse
watercourse availability/legality evidence where infiltration is not reasonably practicable
sewer availability/connection evidence where preceding routes are not reasonably practicable
priorityOrder: adequate soakaway or other adequate infiltration system
watercourse where infiltration is not reasonably practicable
sewer where neither preceding route is reasonably practicable
obligations.nonClaim: A garden is not infiltration evidence, and the statutory priority is not converted into a guessed site route.

obligations.title: Building / underpinning work affecting mapped drain, sewer or disposal main
requiredInputs: actual site/building relationship to mapped asset
obligations.nonClaim: A marketing or planning drainage line is not automatically the statutory map-of-sewers evidence referenced by H4.

obligations.title: Separate foul and surface-water systems where the H5 conditions apply
requiredInputs: whether H3 rainwater will discharge to sewer
whether direct/indirect discharge to the separate surface-water sewer is reasonably practicable
obligations.nonClaim: H5 is not represented as a universal ban on combined drainage independent of its statutory application conditions.

externalRegimeEdges.reason: Public-sewer connection rights/notice/undertaker law are separate from the Building Regulations adequacy obligation.
Environmental permitting/general binding rules remain a separate authority where a non-mains small sewage discharge is proposed.

delegatedSiblingScope.reason: Solid-waste storage/access is not a water/waste-water obligation and should be modelled with external-access/refuse/planning work rather than pulled into this vertical merely because it shares Part H.

Sanitary appliance/hot-water/water-efficiency requirements remain outside this packet. DPL-09C consumes only the fact that H1 drains foul water from relevant appliances; it does not become a full Part G implementation.

currentReferenceHouseDisposition.reason: Building-side service handoff exists, but no evidenced external sewer/non-mains route, levels or competent drainage design is admitted.
Applicability cannot be resolved until the lawful/practicable foul-disposal route is evidenced.
RH-08/DRW provide strong architectural topology evidence, not hydraulic sizing or external receiving-route proof.
Applicable paved-area extent and final access/surface drainage design are not yet fixed.
No infiltration, watercourse or sewer route has evidence sufficient to establish the statutory priority outcome.
No authoritative mapped-sewer/site-interference evidence is admitted for the Reference Site.
Surface-water sewer route and statutory H5 application conditions are not evidenced.
